blocks.text: In Tunisia, *Immigrant Blankets* are part of a familiar landscape. These popular blankets, recognizable by their patterns and colors, belong to the domestic sphere and to everyday culture. In this series, I photograph these blankets because they appear in outdoor spaces, in an almost ordinary everyday gesture, where a fragment of intimacy suddenly finds itself exposed not only to the sunlight, but also to the gaze of others. Hung from windows and balconies, they appear as silent presences, suspended between interior and exterior, intimacy and public space. The term *Immigrant Blanket* evokes displacement and migration. These familiar and comforting objects can accompany those who leave, carrying with them something of their everyday life, their home, and their history. In Tunisia, their presence can also resonate with the different migratory journeys that cross the country today. In my photographs, they take on an almost pictorial dimension. Suspended in often chaotic, grey, or rather dreary urban environments, they appear as touches of color, warmth, and life. They punctuate the landscape like simple and familiar signs of human presence, of somewhere else, or of a place one carries with them.
